subject: physics
question_text: A force of 10 N is applied to a copper wire of diameter 1 mm. Calculate the stress produced in it.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 9 Very Short Answer Question 2 (printed p.98). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: d = 1 mm gives r = 0.5 × 10⁻³ m, A = πr² = 7.85 × 10⁻⁷ m², stress = F/A = 10 / (7.85 × 10⁻⁷) = 1.27 × 10⁷ N m⁻², arithmetic verified.

insider_note: The area calculation is graded separately from the final value — a wrong final answer with the correct area shown still earns the first mark.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Area of cross-section
steps.margin_note: Convert the diameter to radius before squaring — a common slip is squaring the diameter instead.
steps.why: The cross-sectional area is what carries the force, so it must be found before the stress can be calculated.
common_mistakes: Using the diameter directly in A = πr² instead of first halving it to get the radius.
Forgetting the ×10⁻³ when converting mm to m.
steps.memory_tip: Radius is half the diameter — halve first, then square.

steps.label: Stress value
steps.margin_note: State the final value with its power of ten and unit — a bare number without N m⁻² loses this mark.
steps.why: Dividing the given force by the area found in the previous step gives the stress directly from its defining formula.
common_mistakes: Losing track of the negative exponent and reporting the answer as 1.27 × 10⁻⁷.
Omitting the unit N m⁻² after the numeric value.
steps.memory_tip: Now use σ = F/A with the given force and the area just found.
